title: Clinical Trial Indicates A.I. Chatbots Could Aid Urgent Care
source_used: Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center release via Newswise (matching study; NYT page blocked)
key_facts: BIDMC researchers, with Google, ran what they believe is the first prospective real-world study of a patient-facing conversational AI in primary care; findings appear in The Lancet.

The chatbot, AMIE (Articulate Medical Intelligence Explorer), questioned patients by text from home after they booked an urgent primary care appointment, took histories, suggested possible diagnoses and wrote a summary for the doctor.
114 patients enrolled between April and November 2025; 98 finished both the AI chat and the appointment.

A physician watched every chat in real time; none of the 98 completed conversations needed a safety-stop intervention; one hallucination and five cases needing extra clinical clarification were logged.

For the 44 cases where doctors read the AI summary, 75% said it helped them prepare and 57% said it may have influenced their approach; one doctor called it somewhat harmful because a lymphoma mention may have caused anxiety.
Patients worried about confidentiality and about the chatbot's honesty and trustworthiness.
The study tested feasibility, not whether AI improves outcomes; it was funded by Alphabet and lead author Adam Rodman was a visiting researcher at Google during part of it.
quote_evidence: Across all 98 completed encounters, none of the conversations required a safety-stop intervention.
Rodman and colleagues emphasized that the study was designed to evaluate feasibility rather than to determine whether AI improves health outcomes.
why_it_matters_hint: First real-world check that a patient-facing chatbot can run safely under physician watch.
event_date: Study April-November 2025; published in The Lancet, reported 8 Oct 2026
notes: The New York Times page (pool item) returned 403. Matched by topic and date (NYT headline 8 Oct 2026: AI chatbots could aid urgent care) to the BIDMC/Lancet AMIE study; the NYT text could not be checked, so that match is an inference. Credit goes to BIDMC via Newswise.
